b: The single most important factor in learning is whether the student is actively engaged in the process.
Eyes bright, hands up, curious and eager for the insight on the other side.
Ask any teacher–students like this are a delight.
The same is true for the work of professionals–from doctors to cashiers. Wanting to be there, open to interaction, eager for change–these are so obvious that we usually overlook them.
In fact, the real work of anyone building an institution of learning or an organization that seeks to serve is simple: create the conditions for people to choose to actively participate.

The lazy method is to wait for the self-motivated and take credit for the results when they show up. The hard work is to build the systems and culture that makes it more likely that you’re attracting, motivating and transforming the people who want to go where you can take them.
